scale.note: 10 px = 1 in. Every canvas and keep-out is in these px, measured from the LEFT edge as you face the wall and UP from the floor. Photoshop y from top = canvas height minus y from floor.

base_trim.status: Tripp's working value, 8 in (his note on the 10-07 panorama). No tape survey is planned: designs work to true measurements and ratios and an inch either way is fine. Other readings: 4 in on the Zone 4 hallway (M9 / C1) sheet; about 7 in off the M7 photo. One constant (BASE) in index.html.
base_trim.rule: Every wall has a white bottom trim from the floor up to 80 px. It is not paintable and it is its own layer, laid over the wall photo and the design, so a photo that already shows the trim and one that does not end up the same. It breaks at every doorway (together with the door casing) and runs under windows. Anything that stands on the trim, like the B4 mirrors, starts at its top edge, 80 px up, never at the floor.

layers.what: Transparent PNG overlays at the exact canvas px, one per wall plus one per Wall 4 section. Stack them over a design to check it. Do not paint them into a design.
layers.trim: layers/trim/<file id>.png, every wall and every Wall 4 section
layers.mirrors: layers/mirrors/<file id>.png, Wall 4 (M4-B4) and the B4 sections only
layers.doors: layers/doors/<file id>.png, every wall with a door: each door and its casing cut out of the wall photo at canvas px, transparent elsewhere. kind 'door' entries are cut out of the wall in the 3D model; layers/doors/<file id>.png holds them cut from the wall photo
layers.sections: layers/sections/<file id>.png, Wall 4 and each of its sections: the pink dotted section lines and SECTION n tags
layers.file_id: the wall or section id with + written as - (M4+B4 becomes M4-B4). B2's trim layer is cut to the B2 wall-face canvas.
layers.built_by: tools/make_layers.py, from this spec. Never hand-edit; rerun it after make_spec.py.
layers.stack_order: wall photo, then design, then doors, trim and mirrors, then the pink section guides on top

orientation: Left and right are as seen standing in the room facing the wall. The band walks B2 > B3 > M4 > B4 > M7 > M8; the canvases join end to end in that order.
vocabulary: Every wall has three names that mean the same thing: the wall number (Wall 4), the section (Wall 4 Section 2) and the alias id (B4-1). Accept any; answer with all three. Write 'Section', never the section symbol.

delivery.format: PNG with a transparent background, sRGB
delivery.extent: full image width = the wall or section's full length, left edge = the named left corner or split line; full image height = the full wall height. Never crop to the band alone: where the band sits in the height is part of the design.
delivery.size: either the exact canvas px, or the exact ratio at the largest size the tool allows, with the delivered px stated
delivery.keepouts: for the designer's eye only; the 3D model cuts the openings and lays the bottom trim and the mirrors over the design automatically, so a band may run straight across a window or behind a mirror. Keep focal elements out of the doors, the mirrors and the bottom trim.
delivery.corners: a design that turns an inside corner is two files that share the corner edge, column for column
delivery.flat_splits: the M4 / B4 line and the B4 section lines are not corners; neighbouring sections must be continuous across the line

rules: Real scale controls artwork placement. Never deform a wall to fit art.
Do not regenerate the existing M4 mural.
White window and door trim is not paintable.
The bottom trim is not paintable. Mirrors and anything else standing on it start at its top edge, not at the floor.
B4 is the B4 Mirror Band. B5 is the box-face band over M6, a different wall.
M4 and B4 are the same wall.
Do not present provisional values as measured; carry each status string forward.
Do not rename walls or sections; use the names here and raise naming questions with Tripp.
